# Summary

This is an internal replication of Lesly Simbaña's analysis to verify elimination using IgG serology. 

# Preamble

```{r preamble}
library(here)
here()
#----------------------------
# source the config file
#----------------------------
source(here("R","0-config.R"))

```

# Load the Luminex IgG data

```{r load antibody data}
#-------------------------------
# load the formatted MBA data
# for EcoMID, created by
# 0-all_sero_results_dataclean.Rmd
#
# data are in long format
#-------------------------------
d <- read_rds(here("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/EcoMid/data/serology/final/ecomid_serology_datasets","ecomid_sero_antigen_seropos_long_v02_20261007.rds"))
```

```{r process antibody data}
#-------------------------------
# filter to antigens of interest
# pivot wider to make composite
# indicators
#-------------------------------
d1 <- d %>%
  filter( antigen %in% c("ov16","rp17","tmpa","pgp3")) %>%
  select(community_type,childid,timepoint,antigen, seropos) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols=c(community_type,childid,timepoint),names_from = "antigen", values_from = "seropos") %>%
  mutate(oncho=ov16,
         trachoma = pgp3,
         yaws = ifelse(rp17 == 1 & tmpa==1, 1, 0)         
         ) 

#-------------------------------
# pivot pathogen-specific summaries
# back to long format
#-------------------------------
d2 <- d1 %>%
  select(community_type,childid,timepoint,oncho,trachoma,yaws) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols=c(oncho,trachoma,yaws), names_to = "pathogen", values_to = "seropos")

# safety check 
d2 %>% distinct(childid, community_type) %>%
  count(community_type) %>%
  arrange(community_type)
```

# Estimate seroprevalence

```{r estimate seroprevalence overall and by community type}

# identify number of samples
# with missing values
table(d2$pathogen,is.na(d2$seropos))

#-------------------------------
# estimate seroprevalence overall
#-------------------------------
dprev <- d2 %>%
  group_by(pathogen) %>%
  summarize(
    nobs = sum(!is.na(seropos)),
    npos = sum(seropos, na.rm=TRUE)
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    seroprev = (npos/nobs)*100,
    seroprev_min95 = binom.test(x=npos,n=nobs)$conf.int[1]*100,
    seroprev_max95 = binom.test(x=npos,n=nobs)$conf.int[2]*100
  )

kbl(dprev, digits=1)

#-------------------------------
# estimate seroprevalence by
# community type for trachoma pgp3
#-------------------------------
dprev_pgp3_community <- d2 %>%
  filter(pathogen == "trachoma") %>%
  group_by(community_type, pathogen) %>%
  summarize(
    nobs = sum(!is.na(seropos)),
    npos = sum(seropos, na.rm=TRUE)
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    seroprev = (npos/nobs)*100,
    seroprev_min95 = binom.test(x=npos,n=nobs)$conf.int[1]*100,
    seroprev_max95 = binom.test(x=npos,n=nobs)$conf.int[2]*100
  )
  
kbl(dprev_pgp3_community, digits=1)
```

# Estimate child-level seroprevalence for Table 2

The table above counts each measurement (a child can contribute up to 6 visits) as a separate observation. Here we instead count each child once per pathogen: a child is "ever positive" if they were seropositive at *any* visit during follow-up. N children is the number of children with at least one non-missing result for that pathogen; N ever seropositive is how many of those were positive at
least once.

```{r child level pathogen prevalence}
#-------------------------------
# child-level: N children, N
# ever seropositive per pathogen
# at any visit, crude prevalence
# with binomial exact 95% CI
#-------------------------------
d2_child <- d2 %>%
  filter(!is.na(seropos)) %>%
  group_by(childid, pathogen) %>%
  summarize(ever_pos = max(seropos), .groups = "drop")

dprev_child <- d2_child %>%
  group_by(pathogen) %>%
  summarize(
    n_children = n(),
    n_ever_pos = sum(ever_pos),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    child_seroprev = (n_ever_pos/n_children)*100,
    child_seroprev_min95 = binom.test(x=n_ever_pos, n=n_children)$conf.int[1]*100,
    child_seroprev_max95 = binom.test(x=n_ever_pos, n=n_children)$conf.int[2]*100
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(child_seroprev_print = paste0(sprintf("%1.1f",child_seroprev)," (",sprintf("%1.1f",child_seroprev_min95)," to ",sprintf("%1.1f",child_seroprev_max95),")"))

kbl(dprev_child %>% select(pathogen, n_children, n_ever_pos, child_seroprev_print), digits=1,
    col.names = c("Pathogen","N children","N ever seropositive","Child-level seroprevalence (95% CI)"))
```

## Table 2, sample-level and child-level stacked vertically

As with Table 3 below, stack sample-level and child-level estimates into one long table sharing common
column names ("N tested" = N measurements for sample-level, N children for child-level; "N positive";
"Seroprevalence (95% CI)"), grouped by level with `kableExtra::pack_rows()`.

```{r combine table2 sample and child level long}
#-------------------------------
# format sample-level estimates
# for printing, then reshape
# sample-level and child-level
# estimates into a single long
# table sharing common column
# names, so they stack vertically
# instead of side by side
#-------------------------------
dprev_print <- dprev %>%
  mutate(seroprev_print = paste0(sprintf("%1.1f",seroprev)," (",sprintf("%1.1f",seroprev_min95)," to ",sprintf("%1.1f",seroprev_max95),")"))

dprev_long <- bind_rows(
  dprev_print %>%
    transmute(pathogen, level = "Sample-level", n_tested = nobs, n_pos = npos, prev_print = seroprev_print),
  dprev_child %>%
    transmute(pathogen, level = "Child-level", n_tested = n_children, n_pos = n_ever_pos, prev_print = child_seroprev_print)
) %>%
  mutate(
    level = factor(level, levels = c("Sample-level","Child-level")),
    pathogen = factor(pathogen, levels = c("trachoma","oncho","yaws"),
                       labels = c("Trachoma, C. trachomatis (Pgp3)",
                                  "Onchocerciasis, O. volvulus (Ov16)",
                                  "Yaws, T. pallidum (rp17, TmpA)"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(level, pathogen)

tbl2_long <- dprev_long %>%
  select(pathogen, n_tested, n_pos, prev_print)

kbl(tbl2_long, digits=3,
    col.names = c("Disease, pathogen (antigens)","N tested","N positive","Seroprevalence (95% CI)"),
    caption = "Table 2. Seroprevalence to three pathogens assessed for elimination -- sample-level and child-level (ever positive at any visit)") %>%
  pack_rows("Sample-level (per measurement)", 1, sum(dprev_long$level=="Sample-level")) %>%
  pack_rows("Child-level (ever positive at any visit)", sum(dprev_long$level=="Sample-level")+1, nrow(dprev_long))

write_csv(dprev_long, file = here("output","ecomid_table2_seroprev_sample_and_child_level.csv"))
```

## Supp table, community-level prevalence 

At the child-level, summarise  "Seroprevalence (95% CI)") for onchocerciasis and yws 

```{r}
#-------------------------------
# format sample-level estimates
# for printing, then reshape
# sample-level and child-level
# estimates into a single long
# table sharing common column
# names, so they stack vertically
# instead of side by side
#-------------------------------
d_comm <- d %>%
  filter( antigen %in% c("ov16","rp17","tmpa","pgp3")) %>%
  select(community_name,childid,timepoint,antigen, seropos) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols=c(community_name,childid,timepoint),names_from = "antigen", values_from = "seropos") %>%
  mutate(oncho=ov16,
         trachoma = pgp3,
         yaws = ifelse(rp17 == 1 & tmpa==1, 1, 0)         
         ) 

d3 <- d_comm %>%
  select(community_name,childid,timepoint,oncho,trachoma,yaws) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols=c(oncho,trachoma,yaws), names_to = "pathogen", values_to = "seropos")

community_prevalence <- d3 %>%
  filter(!is.na(seropos)) %>%
  group_by(childid, pathogen, community_name) %>%
  summarize(ever_pos = max(seropos), .groups = "drop")

dprev_comm <- community_prevalence %>%
  group_by(pathogen, community_name) %>%
  summarize(
    n_comm = n(),
    n_ever_pos = sum(ever_pos),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    comm_seroprev = (n_ever_pos/n_comm)*100,
    comm_seroprev_min95 = binom.test(x=n_ever_pos, n=n_comm)$conf.int[1]*100,
    comm_seroprev_max95 = binom.test(x=n_ever_pos, n=n_comm)$conf.int[2]*100
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(comm_seroprev_print = paste0(sprintf("%1.1f",comm_seroprev)," (",sprintf("%1.1f",comm_seroprev_min95)," to ",sprintf("%1.1f",comm_seroprev_max95),")"))


# Format table
kbl(dprev_comm  %>% select(community_name, pathogen, n_comm, n_ever_pos, comm_seroprev_print), digits=1,
    col.names = c("Community", "Pathogen","N children","N ever seropositive","Community-level seroprevalence (95% CI)"))

dprev_comm_export <- dprev_comm  %>%
  mutate(community_type = case_when(community_name == "Borbon" ~ "Borbón", 
                                    community_name == "Esmeraldas" ~ "Esmeraldas",
                                    community_name == "Maldonado" ~ "Rural road",
                                    community_name == "Timbire" ~ "Rural road",
                                    community_name == "Selva Alegre" ~ "Rural road",
                                    community_name == "Colon Eloy" ~ "Rural road",
                                    community_name == "Zancudo" ~ "Rural river",
                                    community_name == "Santo Domingo" ~ "Rural river",
                                    community_name == "Colon de Onzole" ~ "Rural river",
                                    community_name == "San Francisco" ~ "Rural river",
                                    )) %>%
  select(pathogen, community_type, community_name, n_comm, n_ever_pos, comm_seroprev_print) 
dprev_comm_export$community_type <- factor(dprev_comm_export$community_type, 
                            levels = c("Esmeraldas", "Borbón", 
                                       "Rural road", "Rural river"))

dprev_comm_export <- dprev_comm_export %>% arrange(pathogen, community_type, community_name)




write_csv(dprev_comm_export, file = here("output","ecomid_supptable_seroprev_community_level.csv"))
```


# Estimate Pgp3 diff by community type

```{r}
#| label: estimate pgp3 seropos diff by community type

options(knitr.kable.NA = '')

#----------------------------
# filter to just trachoma
#----------------------------
d3 <- d2 %>%
  filter(pathogen == "trachoma")
  

#----------------------------
# Estimate differences by
# community type using a 
# linear binomial model
# with robust SEs clustered
# at the child level
#----------------------------

pgp3fit <- glm(seropos ~ community_type, family=binomial(link="identity"), data=d3)
# adjust SEs for repeated measures within child
pgp3fit_rb <- coeftest(pgp3fit, .vcov = vcovCL(pgp3fit, cluster=d3$childid))
pgp3fit_ci <- confint(pgp3fit_rb)

pgp3fit_rb
pgp3fit_ci

#----------------------------
# collate estimates and add
# to seroprevalence table
# multiply difference in 
# proportion by 100 for %
#----------------------------
d_pgp3diffs <- data.frame(
  community_type = c("Esmeraldas","Borbon","Rural Road","Rural River"),
  diff    = c(NA,pgp3fit_rb[2:4,1])*100,
  diff_se = c(NA,pgp3fit_rb[2:4,2])*100,
  diff_p  = c(NA,pgp3fit_rb[2:4,4]),
  diff_min95 = c(NA,pgp3fit_ci[2:4,1])*100,
  diff_max95 = c(NA,pgp3fit_ci[2:4,2])*100
)

dprev_pgp3_community2 <- dprev_pgp3_community %>%
  left_join(d_pgp3diffs, join_by(community_type)) %>%
  # format the differences and prevalence estimates for printing
  mutate(
    seroprev_print = paste0(sprintf("%1.1f",seroprev)," (",sprintf("%1.1f",seroprev_min95)," to ",sprintf("%1.1f",seroprev_max95),")"),
    diff_print = paste0(sprintf("%1.1f",diff)," (",sprintf("%1.1f",diff_min95)," to ",sprintf("%1.1f",diff_max95),")"),
    diff_print = ifelse(is.na(diff),NA,diff_print)
  )

kbl(dprev_pgp3_community2 %>% select(community_type,nobs,npos,seroprev_print,diff_print,diff_p), digits=3, col.names = c("Community type","N measurements","N pos","Seroprevalence (95% CI)","Difference (95% CI)","P-value"))

```

# Estimate Pgp3 child-level prevalence

The table above counts each measurement (a child can contribute up to 6 visits) as a separate
observation. Here we instead count each child once: a child is "ever positive" if they were
seropositive to Pgp3 at *any* visit during follow-up. N children is the number of children with at
least one non-missing Pgp3 result; N ever seropositive is how many of those were positive at least once.

```{r child level pgp3 prevalence}
#-------------------------------
# child-level: N children, N
# ever seropositive to Pgp3 at
# any visit, crude prevalence
# with binomial exact 95% CI
#-------------------------------
d3_child <- d3 %>%
  filter(!is.na(seropos)) %>%
  group_by(childid, community_type) %>%
  summarize(ever_pos = max(seropos), .groups = "drop")

dprev_pgp3_child <- d3_child %>%
  group_by(community_type) %>%
  summarize(
    n_children = n(),
    n_ever_pos = sum(ever_pos),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    child_seroprev = (n_ever_pos/n_children)*100,
    child_seroprev_min95 = binom.test(x=n_ever_pos, n=n_children)$conf.int[1]*100,
    child_seroprev_max95 = binom.test(x=n_ever_pos, n=n_children)$conf.int[2]*100
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(child_seroprev_print = paste0(sprintf("%1.1f",child_seroprev)," (",sprintf("%1.1f",child_seroprev_min95)," to ",sprintf("%1.1f",child_seroprev_max95),")"))

kbl(dprev_pgp3_child %>% select(community_type, n_children, n_ever_pos, child_seroprev_print), digits=1,
    col.names = c("Community type","N children","N ever seropositive","Child-level seroprevalence (95% CI)"))
```

## Estimate child-level Pgp3 diff by community type

Same model as the sample-level difference above (`glm(..., family=binomial(link="identity"))`), but
fit to the child-level "ever positive" outcome. No clustering is needed here since each child
contributes exactly one row already (unlike the sample-level model, which clusters on childid to
account for up to 6 repeated measurements per child) -- we still call `vcovCL(..., cluster=childid)`
for consistency with the code above, but with one row per child this is numerically identical to a
plain heteroskedasticity-robust (HC) sandwich estimator.

```{r child level pgp3 diff by community}
child_fit <- glm(ever_pos ~ community_type, family=binomial(link="identity"), data=d3_child)
child_fit_rb <- coeftest(child_fit, .vcov = vcovCL(child_fit, cluster = d3_child$childid))
child_fit_ci <- confint(child_fit_rb)

child_fit_rb
child_fit_ci

d_childdiffs <- data.frame(
  community_type = c("Esmeraldas","Borbon","Rural Road","Rural River"),
  child_diff    = c(NA,child_fit_rb[2:4,1])*100,
  child_diff_p  = c(NA,child_fit_rb[2:4,4]),
  child_diff_min95 = c(NA,child_fit_ci[2:4,1])*100,
  child_diff_max95 = c(NA,child_fit_ci[2:4,2])*100
)

dprev_pgp3_child <- dprev_pgp3_child %>%
  left_join(d_childdiffs, join_by(community_type)) %>%
  mutate(
    child_diff_print = paste0(sprintf("%1.1f",child_diff)," (",sprintf("%1.1f",child_diff_min95)," to ",sprintf("%1.1f",child_diff_max95),")"),
    child_diff_print = ifelse(is.na(child_diff),NA,child_diff_print)
  )

kbl(dprev_pgp3_child %>% select(community_type, n_children, n_ever_pos, child_seroprev_print, child_diff_print, child_diff_p), digits=3,
    col.names = c("Community type","N children","N ever seropositive","Child-level seroprevalence (95% CI)","Difference (95% CI)","P-value"))
```

## Table 3, sample-level and child-level stacked vertically

Rather than sample-level and child-level side by side, stack them into one long table sharing common
column names ("N tested" = N measurements for sample-level, N children for child-level; "N positive";
"Prevalence (95% CI)"), grouped by level with `kableExtra::pack_rows()`. Difference/P-value now appear
for both levels -- sample-level compares community types on a per-measurement basis (clustered SEs for
repeated visits), child-level compares them on the "ever positive" outcome (one row per child, so no
clustering needed, but the same robust-SE machinery is used).

```{r combine table3 sample and child level long}
#-------------------------------
# reshape sample-level and
# child-level estimates into a
# single long table sharing
# common column names, so they
# stack vertically instead of
# side by side
#-------------------------------
dprev_pgp3_long <- bind_rows(
  dprev_pgp3_community2 %>%
    transmute(community_type, level = "Sample-level",
              n_tested = nobs, n_pos = npos,
              prev_print = seroprev_print,
              diff_print = diff_print, diff_p = diff_p),
  dprev_pgp3_child %>%
    transmute(community_type, level = "Child-level",
              n_tested = n_children, n_pos = n_ever_pos,
              prev_print = child_seroprev_print,
              diff_print = child_diff_print, diff_p = child_diff_p)
) %>%
  # community_type gets silently coerced to a plain character column earlier
  # (the left_join against d_pgp3diffs above joins a factor against a character
  # column of the same name, and the join result drops the factor). Re-impose
  # the intended display order explicitly here rather than relying on
  # whatever type/order survived upstream, otherwise arrange() below sorts
  # community types alphabetically (Borbon, Esmeraldas, Rural River, Rural
  # Road) instead of matching the rest of the manuscript's tables.
  mutate(
    level = factor(level, levels = c("Sample-level","Child-level")),
    community_type = factor(community_type, levels = c("Esmeraldas","Borbon","Rural Road","Rural River"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(level, community_type)

tbl3_long <- dprev_pgp3_long %>%
  select(community_type, n_tested, n_pos, prev_print, diff_print, diff_p)

kbl(tbl3_long, digits=3,
    col.names = c("Community type","N tested","N positive","Prevalence (95% CI)","Difference (95% CI)","P-value"),
    caption = "Table 3. C. trachomatis Pgp3 seroprevalence by community type -- sample-level and child-level (ever positive at any visit)") %>%
  pack_rows("Sample-level (per measurement)", 1, sum(dprev_pgp3_long$level=="Sample-level")) %>%
  pack_rows("Child-level (ever positive at any visit)", sum(dprev_pgp3_long$level=="Sample-level")+1, nrow(dprev_pgp3_long))

write_csv(dprev_pgp3_long, file = here("output","ecomid_table3_pgp3_seroprev_sample_and_child_level.csv"))
```
